correctness.rationale: For any missing edge uv and H=P−J, H1=0 and ⟨e_u−1/n,H(e_v−1/n)⟩=−1/n imply ||H||≥1/(n−1). Equality simultaneously at every nonedge forces H(e_v−1/n)=−(e_u−1/n)/(n−1), impossible when two nonedges share v; thus complement matching necessary. For any k missing disjoint pairs and m unmatched vertices the explicitly specified P (a=1/(n−1) on allowed entries touching a matched vertex, b=(m−1)/[m(n−1)] within unmatched class when m>0) is symmetric stochastic nonnegative, and full invariant-space decomposition has spectrum {1,a,−a,0}, proving equality. Compact feasibility gives strict inequality for any nonmatching complement. Includes m=0,1 boundary cases and disconnected graphs. Independent exact rational 63 n,k cases checked; general proof is analytic.
